cse-2019-cs-15.approach: A pumping length $p$ must make **every** string of length $\ge p$ pumpable. The string $b^{10}$ cannot be pumped at all, so $p > 10$; then check that 24 works.

steps.title: Strings of L
steps.body: $a$-strings: lengths $2, 5, 8, 11, \dots$ ($\equiv 2 \bmod 3$). $b$-strings: lengths $10, 22, 34, \dots$ ($\equiv 10 \bmod 12$, at least 10).

steps.title: b^10 cannot be pumped
steps.body: Pumping $y = b^j$ ($1 \le j \le 10$) down ($i=0$) gives $b^{10-j}$ of length $< 10$, which is not in $L$. So any valid $p$ must exceed 10, ruling out 3, 5 and 9.

steps.title: 24 works
steps.body:
Strings with length $\ge 24$: $a^{2+3k}$ ($k \ge 8$): take $y = aaa$; $a^{2+3(k+i-1)}$ stays in $L$ for all $i \ge 0$ since $k-1 \ge 0$.

$b^{10+12k}$ with $k \ge 2$ (length $\ge 34$): take $y = b^{12}$ within the first 24 symbols; $i=0$ gives $b^{10+12(k-1)}$, still in $L$.

So $p = 24$ satisfies the lemma.

optionAnalysis.reason: With $p=3$ the string $b^{10}$ (length 10 ≥ 3) would have to be pumpable, but it is not.
Same problem: $b^{10}$ has length $\ge 5$ and cannot be pumped.
$b^{10}$ has length $\ge 9$ and cannot be pumped.
Every string of length $\ge 24$ can be pumped with $y = a^3$ or $y = b^{12}$.

pitfalls: Picking the smallest number that works for the a-part (3) and forgetting that b^10 must also be pumpable when p ≤ 10.
cse-2019-cs-15.verification: Options 3, 5 and 9 are all $\le 10$, so they fail on $b^{10}$; for $p = 24$ every long string has a valid pump ($a^3$ or $b^{12}$), as shown.

cse-2019-cs-31.approach: A PDA can match only nested (last-in-first-out) dependencies. In (C) the $w \ldots w^R$ pair and the $a^n \ldots b^n$ pair cross each other, which one stack cannot handle.

steps.body:
(A) even palindromes: $S \to aSa \mid bSb \mid \epsilon$.

(B) $w\,a^nb^n\,w^R$: nested — $S \to aSa \mid bSb \mid T,\ T \to aTb \mid \epsilon$.

(D) union of $\{a^nb^n\}, \{a^nb^{3n}\}, \{a^nb^{5n}\}$, each context-free, and CFLs are closed under union.

steps.title: C is not
steps.body:
In $w\,a^n\,w^R\,b^n$ the block $a^n$ must be matched with $b^n$ **across** $w^R$, while $w$ must be matched with $w^R$ **across** $a^n$. These two dependencies cross, and a single stack can only check nested (LIFO) matchings: after pushing $w$ and then counting $a^n$, the PDA must pop $w$ before it can reach the $a$-count.

A CFL pumping-lemma argument on a long witness (e.g. $w = (ab)^p$, $n = p$) makes this rigorous: a pump window of length $\le p$ cannot change both crossing pairs consistently. So C is not context-free.

The a^n b^n block sits inside the w … w^R nesting, so a single stack handles it.
Correct: the two matchings cross, so no PDA can recognise it.
A finite union of the CFLs {a^n b^n}, {a^n b^{3n}}, {a^n b^{5n}} is a CFL.
